messages:
Priya: FYI customer acct 7632 reporting sudden 429 spikes and 200-400ms tail latency from EU. They say traffic is landing in us-west. Sample request_id: r_0a9f3c. Can someone confirm routing?
Marco: On it. Do we have a sample client IP or at least the edge IP they hit?
Priya: Customer pasted this in support: curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" --data '{"prompt":"hi"}'
Priya: They also ran `dig` and saw an A for a us-west pop instead of FRA. Said ISP resolver might be returning stale answer.
dns-bot: Automated check: queried authoritative geoip mapping for the hostname from our controlplane. Result: preferred region=eu-central, fallback=us-west when edns-client-subnet absent. TTL=300.
Marco: Can you paste the customer's `dig +trace` output? if their resolver strips EDNS/Client-Subnet, many CDNs will return a different POP.
Priya: They posted this snippet: ```;; QUESTION SECTION:
api.redwood.example. IN A
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood.example. 300 IN A 34.223.11.45  ; us-west
;; OPT PSEUDOSECTION: ; EDNS: version: 0, flags:; udp: 1232```
Marco: That OPT shows no ECS. Looks like their resolver is not supplying client subnet. If resolver is in US, geoip will map to US pop -> auth tokens then routed through us-west, hitting rate limits there -> 429s.
Alex: Checked routing logs for r_0a9f3c: decision path -> region policy: prefer-region=eu; resolver_probe: us-west answer -> applied fallback_policy: cross-region-allow, selected us-west. Latency path shows extra 180ms due to cross-region hop.
Priya: Is this an infra bug or expected behavior? Customer expects EU routing.
Marco: This is expected when resolver hides ECS. Not a bug in runtime. But we should make mitigations: 1) shorten fallback TTL or 2) honor region pin headers from SDK or 3) expose a per-account region override to avoid fallback.
Alex: Short-term: we can push a hotfix to lower fallback window from 10m -> 30s for EU customers showing auth anomalies, and add a scoring penalty for cross-region answers when auth scope matches EU tenant. Will schedule if approved.
Priya: Repro steps for SRE to verify: 1) run `dig +noedns api.redwood.example @<customer-resolver>` 2) run `dig +edns=0 +client=203.0.113.12 api.redwood.example @8.8.8.8` 3) curl with `X-Region-Hint: eu` header and compare.
Marco: I repro'd locally by forcing resolver to US via /etc/resolv.conf -> got A for us-west and 429 after ~120s of traffic as tokens hit us cluster.
Priya: Customer asked for quick mitigation while we work on config: suggested they switch to 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8 to see if that fixes. Is it safe to recommend cache flush?
Alex: Yes, advise customer to test with public resolvers and also try `dig +short api.redwood.example @1.1.1.1`. For longer term we'll add a console flag: "sticky_local_region" per-account.
dns-bot: Note: we observed increased resolver-side TTL caching in specific ISP family (AS64500) in last 24h; filed ticket with partners for geoip sync.
Priya: Action items: @Marco to file config PR to lower fallback window for affected EU accounts (ETA 4h). @Alex to add per-account region override RFC. Support to send customer repro steps and ask for dig output and their resolver IP.
Marco: Filing PR now, will link here. :thumbsup:
deploybot: deploy queued for canary config change -> fallback-window-ms=30000 targeting eu cluster.
Priya: I'll message the customer with repro steps and temporary guidance. Thanks team. :smile:
